text: Pillar one of the target architecture needs an actual design, not just a sentence. Mara turns it into real zones, VLANs, and firewall rules she can hand to Hartwell's network team.

Instead of a direct boundary between corporate IT and OT SCADA, she designs three zones. Zone one, corporate IT, stays as-is. Zone two is a new, narrow DMZ jump zone containing only hardened jump boxes — the only path allowed to initiate a connection into zone three. Zone three is the isolated OT SCADA segment, carved onto its own VLAN four forty, on the 10.40.0.0/24 subnet.

On the Azure side, the SCADA gateway subnet's network security group moves from broad corporate access to an explicit allow rule for only the jump zone's address range on port 443, backed by a visible deny-all-inbound rule. On the AWS side, the OT telemetry account gets its own dedicated VPC with a Network Firewall rule group mirroring the same logic: allow only from the jump zone, deny and log everything else.

This plan ships first in monitor-only mode, so Mara can see what the new rules would have blocked before anything actually gets blocked. Next lesson builds pillar two on top of this newly segmented boundary: consolidating Azure and AWS identity into one view.
